pageProps.title: Jini, Genie
pageProps.review: Jeong You-jeong's Jini, Genie looks into the contradictions of the human world through a bonobo and is a work that provides deep life lessons and emotion with a cheerful and warm perspective different from previous works.
pageProps.description: Two souls thrown into a whirlpool of fate, warmly resonating across the boundary between life and death
pageProps.content:
## Review It is a novel with warm and deep lessons by author Jeong You-jeong. The author seems to have an extraordinary attachment to ```animals```. If I felt difficult emotions while reading the descriptions of animals in 28, I felt a bit of a cheerful and lively feeling in this work. It has a slightly different atmosphere from the author's previous works like 28, The Good Son, and Seven Years of Night, and it was new because it's a work that can be viewed without frowning.
The ```bonobo``` is an intentional device with symbolism and biological similarity in mind.
The protagonist returning to a human is not a recovery of the body, but a return to that ```bound human world```. To her, human society must have been an even more violent and standardized space.
